paragraphs: We are a pioneering gene editing company dedicated to developing potentially transformative genomic medicines to treat a broad range of serious diseases. The promise of genomic medicines is supported by the advancing knowledge of the human genome and by harnessing the progress in technologies for cell therapy, gene therapy, and, most recently, gene editing. We believe this progress sets the stage for us to create medicines with the potential to have a durable benefit for patients. Our core capability in gene editing uses the technology known as CRISPR (clustered, regularly interspaced, short palindromic repeats) to allow us to create molecules that efficiently and specifically edit DNA. Our mission is to translate the promise of gene editing into a broad class of differentiated, transformational medicines for previously untreatable diseases.

We have developed a proprietary gene editing platform based on CRISPR technology and we continue to expand its capabilities. CRISPR uses a protein-RNA complex composed of an enzyme, including either Cas9 (CRISPR associated protein 9) or Cas12a (CRISPR from Prevotella and Francisella 1, also known as Cpf1), bound to a guide RNA molecule designed to recognize a particular DNA sequence. Once the complex binds to the DNA sequence it is designed to recognize, the complex makes a specific cut in the DNA. We believe we are the only human gene editing company with a platform that includes CRISPR/Cas9, CRISPR/Cas12a, engineered forms of both of these CRISPR systems, and foundational intellectual property for both of these CRISPR systems. Because of the broad nature of this platform, we believe we can create gene editing molecules for more than 95% of the human genome.

We seek to be a leader in in vivo gene editing, leveraging cutting edge gene editing technology to deliver transformative therapies that simplify the usability for patients, minimize the burdens to patients and healthcare systems, and are meaningfully differentiated from the current standards of care, while also allowing a simple, scalable manufacturing process to reduce costs to manufacture and administer the therapies.

Our approach is focused on the in vivo use of functional upregulation, which aims to increase the expression of a normal gene copy and its normal protein function to treat diseases caused by genetic mutations that eliminate or disrupt normal function. This approach edits non-coding regulatory sequences upstream and downstream of a gene and does not alter the sequence of the encoded protein, unlike other approaches, including gene knockdown, which aims to reduce the expression of one or more targeted genes by editing coding regions to knockdown a disease-causing protein, and gene correction, which aims to edit coding regions to correct a disease-causing protein. We believe this approach will allow us to address those diseases where the gene knockdown approach has limited effectiveness and to create treatments designed for most or all patients with the same disease, regardless of the specific genetic mutation causing the disease.

We believe the ability to provide in vivo gene editing, in which the medicine is injected or infused into the patient to edit the cells inside their body, and functionally upregulate normal gene expression and normal protein function in the target tissues holds the potential to significantly expand the addressable therapeutic possibilities of CRISPR-based gene editing. To that end, our preclinical efforts are also focused on the creation of a "plug ‘n play" lipid nanoparticle ("LNP") platform to enable targeted delivery of in vivo gene editing medicines to multiple cells and tissues, including the liver, hematopoietic stem cells ("HSCs"), and other cells and tissues.

In September 2025, we announced the nomination of our lead in vivo development candidate, EDIT-401, an experimental, potential best-in-class, one-time therapy to significantly reduce LDL-cholesterol ("LDL-C") through upregulation of the LDL receptor ("LDLR"). EDIT-401 is designed to treat elevated levels of LDL-C, or hyperlipidemia, by directly editing the noncoding region of the LDLR gene to increase LDLR protein expression and reduce LDL-C levels. This targeted approach has demonstrated an approximately 90% mean reduction of LDL-C in non-human primates ("NHPs") in our preclinical studies with favorable tolerability data and supports the potential of EDIT-401 to deliver meaningful clinical outcomes for patients underserved by current lipid-lowering therapies. We are on track to submit an investigational new drug application ("IND") or foreign equivalent to conduct a clinical trial of EDIT-401 in patients with heterozygous familial hypercholesteremia ("HeFH"), a common inherited genetic disorder causing extremely high LDL-C, by mid-2026 with the expectation of achieving early human proof-of-concept data for EDIT-401 by the end of 2026. We plan to complete enrolling the dose-finding portion of the first-in-human clinical trial with topline data results available in 2027. We expect to present additional preclinical data for EDIT-401 by mid-2026.

We also previously demonstrated proof-of-concept of our functional upregulation strategy in our former clinical trials of renizgamglogene autogedtemcel ("reni-cel"), an experimental ex vivo gene-edited medicine to treat sickle cell disease ("SCD"), a severe inherited blood disease that causes vaso-occlusive events and target organ damage, and often leads to premature death, and transfusion-dependent beta thalassemia ("TDT"), the most severe form of beta-thalassemia, an inherited blood disorder characterized by severe anemia. Despite the robust and clinically meaningful improvements observed in these trials, we determined in December 2024 not to pursue commercialization for reni-cel in order to optimize our cost structure and accelerate our intent to achieve human proof of concept of our in vivo gene editing medicines. Leveraging our differentiated approach from our former reni-cel program, we are developing an experimental in vivo gene-editing medicine to edit HSCs through targeted delivery of our AsCas12a enzyme to our clinically validated HBG1 and HBG2 promoter site.

Our in vivo discovery and development efforts further include other cells and tissues, with the goal of selecting therapeutic targets we believe have a significant probability of technical, clinical, regulatory, and commercial success. We previously announced in vivo delivery to two additional cell types in humanized mice using our proprietary LNP targeting platform, demonstrating the "plug ‘n play" potential of our proprietary extrahepatic LNP platform.

We are pursuing the right combination of gene editing and targeted delivery tools through internal development and the in-licensing of complementary technologies to build our preclinical pipeline, including our "plug ‘n play" in vivo gene editing LNP delivery platform, and accelerate the achievement of our goal of delivering lifesaving medicines to patients with previously untreatable diseases. For example, we are party to a collaboration and license agreement accessing LNPs targeting the liver in support of our strategy to upregulate certain liver targets, including LDLR for our EDIT-401 program.

We are also leveraging our gene editing technology to drive the development of CRISPR-based medicines in therapeutic areas outside of our core focus through partnerships and collaborations. For example, our collaboration with Bristol Myers Squibb Company ("BMS") through its wholly owned subsidiary, Juno Therapeutics, Inc. ("Juno Therapeutics") is advancing alpha-beta T-cell experimental medicines for the treatment of solid tumors, liquid tumors, and autoimmune disease in collaboration. This collaboration, which leverages our Cas9 and AsCas12a platform technologies, has resulted in 14 total programs, including BMS' CD19 HD Allo CAR T program for the treatment of autoimmune disease currently in Phase I clinical development. We are also party to a non-exclusive collaboration and licensing agreement with Immatics to combine gamma-delta T cell adoptive cell therapies and gene editing for the treatment of cancer.

In addition, we are leveraging our intellectual property portfolio to drive potential out-licensing opportunities that can provide non-dilutive capital. In December 2023, we and Vertex Pharmaceuticals Incorporated ("Vertex") entered into a license agreement (the "Vertex License Agreement"), under which Vertex obtained a non-exclusive license for our Cas9 gene editing technology for ex vivo gene editing medicines targeting the BCL11A gene in the fields of SCD and TDT, including Vertex's CASGEVYTM (exagamglogene autotemcel). We received a $50.0 million upfront cash payment in the fourth quarter of 2023 and the 2024 annual license fee of $10.0 million in the first quarter of 2024. The Vertex License Agreement further provides for the payment by Vertex of a potential additional $50.0 million contingent upfront payment and further future fixed and sales-based annual license fees, ranging from $5.0 million to $40.0 million annually, inclusive of certain sales-based annual license fee increases, through 2034. We are required to pay The Broad Institute, Inc. ("Broad") and the President and Fellows of Harvard College ("Harvard") a mid-double-digit percentage of amounts payable to us from Vertex under the Vertex License Agreement as it relates to Cas9 technology licensed by us from Broad and Harvard. In October 2024, we entered into an agreement (the "DRI Agreement") with a wholly owned subsidiary of DRI Healthcare Trust ("DRI") providing for an upfront cash payment by DRI to us of $57.0 million. Under the DRI Agreement, DRI is purchasing up to 100% of certain future fixed and sales-based annual license fees that the Company is entitled to receive under the Vertex License Agreement, which fees range from $5.0 million to $40.0 million per year, including increases based on sales. In addition, DRI is purchasing a mid-double-digit percentage of a $50.0 million contingent upfront payment that the Company may receive under the Vertex License Agreement. All amounts above will be adjusted to exclude payments that the Company owes to Broad and Harvard. The Company has retained rights to certain portions of certain other sales-based annual license fees and the contingent upfront payment that may become due under the Vertex License Agreement, and the amounts that correspond to our licensor obligations.

Gene editing is the process of revising, removing, or repairing defective DNA in situ. In general, gene editing repairs the defective DNA in its native genomic location, and consequently the repaired genetic region retains the cell's normal control and feedback mechanisms. Gene editing typically takes advantage of naturally occurring DNA repair mechanisms, including non-homologous end joining ("NHEJ") and homology directed repair ("HDR"), to achieve its desired therapeutic outcome. Edits that are repaired by NHEJ typically result in an insertion or deletion (an "indel") that can disrupt a regulatory sequence to functionally upregulate normal gene expression and normal protein function. Edits that are repaired by HDR, including targeted insertion, aim to correct or replace aberrant DNA sequences. The diversity of genetic drivers of disease demands a variety of solutions. Gene editing has the potential to deliver a variety of types of genome modification to address a broad range of diseases.

CRISPR technology uses a protein-RNA complex composed of a type of enzyme, referred to as a DNA endonuclease, bound to an RNA molecule, referred to as a guide RNA, that has been designed to recognize a particular DNA sequence. A DNA endonuclease is an enzyme that cleaves DNA. This combination of a DNA endonuclease and a guide RNA only bind and cut DNA when two criteria are met: first, the protein recognizes a short DNA specific to the enzyme called the protospacer adjacent motif ("PAM"), and second, the appropriate portion of the guide RNA matches the adjacent DNA sequence. The PAM sequence that is recognized by the DNA endonuclease creates a second layer of recognition in addition to the guide RNA. We believe that CRISPR technology has three principal advantages for gene editing:

•Rapid, comprehensive, and systematic identification of product candidates. The key targeting mechanism for the endonuclease, whether it is Cas9 or Cas12a, is a guide RNA, which can be rapidly replaced with a different guide RNA or optimized by changes as small as a single nucleotide. This allows for the flexible design, synthesis, and testing of hundreds of guide RNA/endonuclease combinations for each genetic target in order to find those that cut the DNA target with the optimal efficiency and specificity. In contrast, other commonly used DNA nucleases for gene editing have inherently limited flexibility. For example, zinc finger nucleases, engineered meganucleases, and transcription activator-like effector nucleases use proteins for DNA sequence recognition to bring the endonuclease to the site of the genome where cleavage is desired, requiring the creation of an entirely new protein for each target site.

headings: Risks Related to Our Financial Position and Need for Additional Capital
We have incurred significant losses since inception. We expect to incur losses for the foreseeable future and may never achieve or maintain profitability.

We will need substantial additional funding. If we are unable to raise capital when needed, we would be forced to delay, reduce, or eliminate our research and product development programs or commercialization efforts.
Raising additional capital may cause dilution to our stockholders, restrict our operations or require us to relinquish rights to our technologies or product candidates.
Our operating history may make it difficult for our stockholders to evaluate the success of our business to date and to assess our future viability.
We have never generated revenue from product sales and may never be profitable.
Unfavorable national or global economic conditions or political developments could adversely affect our business, financial condition or results of operations.
Risks Related to Discovery, Development, and Commercialization
Regulatory requirements governing genetic medicines, and in particular any novel genetic medicines we may develop, have changed frequently and may continue to change in the future.
We may not be successful in our efforts to identify, develop, or commercialize potential product candidates.
We have not tested any of our proposed delivery modes, combined with our product candidates, in clinical trials and have not begun clinical trials in any of our current development programs.

We currently plan to conduct and may in the future conduct clinical trials for our product candidates outside the U.S., and the FDA and comparable foreign regulatory authorities may not accept data from such trials.
experience delays in completing, or ultimately be unable to complete, the development and commercialization of such product candidates.

Since inception, we have incurred significant operating losses. Our net losses were $160.1 million, $237.1 million, and $153.2 million for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively. As of December 31, 2025, we had an accumulated deficit of $1.6 billion. We have financed our operations primarily through public offerings of our common stock, our research collaboration with Bristol Myers Squibb Company ("BMS") through its wholly owned subsidiary, Juno Therapeutics, Inc., payments under our former strategic alliance with Allergan Pharmaceuticals International Limited (together with its affiliates, "Allergan"), which was terminated in August 2020, payments received under our purchase and sale agreement with DRI Healthcare Acquisitions LP, and payments under our license agreement with Vertex Pharmaceuticals, Incorporated ("Vertex"). We have devoted substantially all of our efforts to research and development. We expect to continue to incur significant expenses and increasing operating losses for the foreseeable future. The net losses we incur may fluctuate significantly from quarter to quarter. We anticipate that our expenses will increase substantially if and as we:
•continue to support preclinical studies and prepare for the clinical development of EDIT-401;
•initiate and conduct clinical trials of EDIT-401;
•continue our current research programs and our preclinical development of product candidates from our current research programs;
•seek to identify additional product candidates and research programs;

Our operations to date have focused on organizing and staffing our company, business planning, raising capital, establishing our intellectual property portfolio, assembling our core capabilities in gene editing, seeking to identify potential product candidates, and undertaking preclinical studies and clinical trials. All of our ongoing research programs are still in the preclinical or research stage of development and the risk of failure of all of our research programs is high. We have not generated any revenue from product sales. We have primarily financed our operations through various equity financings, payments received under our research collaboration with BMS, our former strategic alliance with Allergan Pharmaceuticals International Limited (together with its affiliates, "Allergan"), which was terminated in August 2020, payments received under the DRI Agreement in connection with the Vertex License Agreement, and payments under the Vertex License Agreement.

Our net losses may fluctuate significantly from quarter to quarter and from year to year. We anticipate that our expenses will increase as we continue to support preclinical studies and prepare for the clinical development of EDIT-401; commence and conduct clinical trials of EDIT-401; continue our current research programs and our preclinical development activities; seek to identify additional research programs and additional product candidates; initiate preclinical testing for other product candidates we identify and develop; maintain, expand, and protect our intellectual property portfolio, including reimbursing our licensors for such expenses related to the intellectual property that we in-license from such licensors; further develop our gene editing platform; and hire personnel. We do not expect to be profitable for the year ending December 31, 2026 or for the foreseeable future.
To date, we have not generated any revenue from product sales and we do not expect to generate any revenue from product sales for the foreseeable future.

In connection with our collaboration with BMS, we have received an aggregate of $159.0 million in payments, which have primarily consisted of the initial upfront and amendment payments, development milestone payments, research funding support, and certain opt-in fees. We no longer receive research funding support. During the year ended December 31, 2025, we recognized $23.2 million of revenue related to our collaboration with BMS of which $9.7 million was previously deferred revenue. As of December 31, 2025, we had $40.5 million of deferred revenue related to BMS, all of which is classified as long-term deferred revenue on our consolidated balance sheet. Under this collaboration, we recognize revenue upon delivery of option packages to BMS or upon receipt of development milestone payments. We expect that our revenue will fluctuate from quarter-to-quarter and year-to-year as a result of the timing of when we deliver such option packages or receive such milestone payments.

Pursuant to the Vertex License Agreement, we received a $50.0 million upfront cash payment in the fourth quarter of 2023 upon execution of the agreement and the 2024 and 2025 annual license fees of $10.0 million in each of the first quarters of 2024 and 2025. The license agreement further provides for the payment by Vertex of a potential additional $50.0 million contingent upfront payment and further annual license fees, ranging from $5.0 million to $40.0 million annually, inclusive of certain sales-based annual license fee increases, through 2034. For the year ended, December 31, 2025, we recorded $10.0 million of revenue related to the annual license fee under the agreement.

headings: 本公司策略
本公司核心能力 —— 基因編輯
本公司基因編輯藥物計畫
本公司合作與授權策略
paragraphs: 本公司為一間先驅性的基因編輯公司，致力於開發具潛力的基因組藥物，用以治療廣泛的嚴重疾病。基因組藥物的潛力由人類基因組知識的進步以及利用細胞治療、基因治療及最近的基因編輯技術的進展所支撐。我們相信這項進展為我們創造具備潛力對患者產生長期效益的藥物奠定了基礎。我們的核心能力在於基因編輯技術，該技術使用稱為 CRISPR（clustered, regularly interspaced, short palindromic repeats）的技術，使我們能夠製造出能高效且具體編輯 DNA 的分子。我們的使命是將基因編輯的潛力轉化為一類差異化、具革命性的藥物，用以治療過去無法治療的疾病。

我們已開發出基於 CRISPR 技術的專有基因編輯平台，並持續擴展其功能。CRISPR 使用由酵素（包括 Cas9（CRISPR associated protein 9）或 Cas12a（CRISPR from Prevotella and Francisella 1，也稱為 Cpf1））與設計用以識別特定 DNA 序列的導向 RNA 分子組成的蛋白質-RNA 組合。一旦該組合與其設計識別的 DNA 序列結合，該組合就會在 DNA 上做出特定的切割。我們相信本公司是唯一一家擁有包含 CRISPR/Cas9、CRISPR/Cas12a、這些 CRISPR 系統的工程化形式，以及這些 CRISPR 系統的基礎智慧財產權的基因編輯公司。由於該平台的廣泛性，我們相信我們可以為人類基因組中超過 95% 的區域開發基因編輯分子。
我們致力於成為體內基因編輯的領導者，利用尖端的基因編輯技術，提供簡化患者使用、減少患者與醫療系統負擔、與現有標準照護有顯著差異的治療方案，同時也允許簡單、可擴充的製造流程，以降低製造與施打治療的費用。

我們的策略聚焦於體內使用功能性基因表達調控，旨在增加正常基因拷貝的表達及其正常蛋白功能，以治療由遺傳變異導致的疾病，這些變異會消除或幹擾正常功能。此方法會編輯基因上游及下游的非編碼調控序列，而不改變編碼蛋白的序列，與其他方法不同，例如基因抑制，旨在透過編輯編碼區域來降低一個或多個目標基因的表達，以抑制致病蛋白，以及基因修復，旨在編輯編碼區域以修復致病蛋白。我們相信此方法將使我們能處理那些基因抑制方法效果有限的疾病，並開發針對大多數或所有患有相同疾病的患者的治療方案，不管造成疾病的特定遺傳變異為何。
我們相信能夠提供體內基因編輯的潛力，即將藥物注射或輸注至患者體內，以編輯體內細胞並功能性調控正常基因表達及正常蛋白功能，這將大幅拓展基於 CRISPR 的基因編輯的治療可能性。為此，我們的預臨牀努力也聚焦於開發一個「即插即用」的脂質奈米粒子（"LNP"）平台，以實現體內基因編輯藥物針對多種細胞和組織的定向遞送，包括肝臟、造血幹細胞（"HSCs"）及其他細胞和組織。

2025 年 9 月，我們宣佈提名我們的體內開發領先候選藥物 EDIT-401，這是一種實驗性、潛力為最佳等級、一次治療的療法，用以顯著降低低密度脂蛋白膽固醇（"LDL-C"），透過調控低密度脂蛋白受體（"LDLR"）的表達。EDIT-401 設計用以治療 LDL-C 水平升高，即高血脂症，透過直接編輯 LDLR 基因的非編碼區域，增加 LDLR 蛋白的表達，並降低 LDL-C 水準。此針對性方法在我們的預臨牀研究中顯示在非人類靈長類動物（"NHPs"）中平均降低 LDL-C 約 90%，並有良好的耐受性數據，支持 EDIT-401 有潛力為現有降血脂療法未充分服務的患者帶來顯著的臨牀結果。我們預計在 2026 年中提交新藥申請（"IND"）或其外國對應文件，以進行 EDIT-401 在患有異質性家族性高膽固醇血癥（"HeFH"）患者的臨牀試驗，HeFH 是一種常見的遺傳性疾病，導致極高的 LDL-C 水準。我們預計在 2026 年底前達成 EDIT-401 的早期人體概念驗證數據。我們計畫在 2027 年完成第一個入體臨牀試驗的劑量尋找部分，並在 2027 年取得初步數據結果。我們預計在 2026 年中展示更多 EDIT-401 的預臨牀數據。

我們也曾在過去的臨牀試驗中展示我們功能性基因表達調控策略的可行性，這些試驗針對的是 renizgamglogene autogedtemcel（"reni-cel"），一種實驗性的體外基因編輯藥物，用以治療地中海貧血（"SCD"），一種嚴重的遺傳性血液疾病，會導致血管阻塞事件及目標器官損傷，並常導致早逝，以及 β-地中海貧血（"TDT"），一種最嚴重的 β-地中海貧血形式，是一種遺傳性血液疾病，特徵為嚴重貧血。儘管這些試驗中觀察到強而有力且臨牀上有意義的改善，我們在 2024 年 12 月決定不追求 reni-cel 的商業化，以優化成本結構並加速我們實現體內基因編輯藥物的人體概念驗證的意圖。利用我們前 reni-cel 程式中差異化的策略，我們正在開發一種實驗性的體內基因編輯藥物，透過針對性遞送我們臨牀驗證的 HBG1 和 HBG2 基因啟動子位點的 AsCas12a 酵素，來編輯 HSCs。
我們的體內發現與開發努力進一步包括其他細胞和組織，目標是選擇我們認為有顯著技術、臨牀、法規及商業成功機率的治療目標。我們先前已宣佈在人類化小鼠中使用我們專有的 LNP 靶向平台，實現對另外兩種細胞類型的體內遞送，展示我們專有的非肝臟 LNP 平台具有「即插即用」的潛力。

本公司正透過內部開發及取得補充性技術的授權，尋求正確的基因編輯與目標遞送工具組合，以建立我們的臨牀前藥物開發管道，包括我們的 "plug ‘n play" 體內基因編輯 LNP 遞送平台，並加速實現我們的目標，即為患有先前無法治療疾病的患者提供救命藥物。例如，本公司為一項合作與授權協議的一方，該協議可取得針對肝臟的 LNPs，以支持我們提升特定肝臟目標的策略，包括 EDIT-401 程式中的 LDLR。

本公司亦透過合作與合作關係，利用我們的基因編輯技術來推動 CRISPR 基因編輯藥物在非核心關注領域的開發。例如，我們與 Bristol Myers Squibb 公司（"BMS"）透過其全資子公司 Juno Therapeutics, Inc.（"Juno Therapeutics"）的合作關係，正在推動 alpha-beta T 細胞實驗性藥物，用以治療實體腫瘤、液體腫瘤及自身免疫疾病。此合作關係利用我們的 Cas9 和 AsCas12a 平台技術，已產生 14 種總計計畫，包括 BMS 的 CD19 HD Allo CAR T 程式，用以治療自身免疫疾病，目前處於第一期臨牀開發階段。本公司亦為一項非獨佔的合作與授權協議的一方，與 Immatics 合作，將 gamma-delta T 細胞過繼細胞治療與基因編輯結合，用以治療癌症。

此外，本公司亦利用我們的智慧財產權組合，推動潛在的出許可機會，以提供非稀釋性資金。2023 年 12 月，本公司與 Vertex Pharmaceuticals Incorporated（"Vertex"）簽訂一項授權協議（"Vertex 授權協議"），根據該協議，Vertex 取得我們的 Cas9 基因編輯技術的非獨佔授權，用以開發針對 BCL11A 基因的 ex vivo 基因編輯藥物，應用於 SCD 和 TDT 領域，包括 Vertex 的 CASGEVYTM（exagamglogene autotemcel）。本公司於 2023 年第四季收到 50.0 百萬美元的預付現金，並於 2024 年第一季收到 2024 年年度授權費 10.0 百萬美元。Vertex 授權協議進一步規定 Vertex 需支付一筆潛在額外 50.0 百萬美元的預付金，以及未來固定的年度授權費及銷售基於的年度授權費，範圍為每年 5.0 百萬至 40.0 百萬美元，包括某些銷售基於的年度授權費增加，至 2034 年為止。本公司需支付 The Broad Institute, Inc.（"Broad"）及 President and Fellows of Harvard College（"Harvard"）一筆中雙位數百分比的金額，該金額為本公司從 Vertex 授權協議中收到的金額，與 Cas9 技術的授權有關，該技術由本公司從 Broad 和 Harvard 授權取得。2024 年 10 月，本公司與 DRI Healthcare Trust 的全資子公司（"DRI"）簽訂一項協議（"DRI 協議"），根據該協議，DRI 向本公司支付 57.0 百萬美元的預付現金。根據 DRI 協議，DRI 購買本公司根據 Vertex 授權協議有權收取的未來固定及銷售基於的年度授權費，該費用每年為 5.0 百萬至 40.0 百萬美元，包括根據銷售情況增加的費用。此外，DRI 購買一筆中雙位數百分比的 50.0 百萬美元潛在預付金，該金額為本公司根據 Vertex 授權協議可能收到的金額。上述所有金額將調整以排除本公司應支付給 Broad 和 Harvard 的金額。本公司保留某些其他銷售基於的年度授權費及潛在預付金的部分權利，該預付金可能根據 Vertex 授權協議而產生，與本公司作為許可人的義務相應的金額。

基因編輯是修復、去除或修復缺陷 DNA 的過程。通常，基因編輯會在 DNA 的原生基因組位置修復缺陷 DNA，因此修復後的遺傳區域會保留細胞的正常控制和反饋機制。基因編輯通常會利用自然發生的 DNA 修復機制，包括非同源端接合（"NHEJ"）和同源導入修復（"HDR"），以達到其所需的治療效果。透過 NHEJ 修復的編輯通常會導致插入或刪除（"indel"），這可能會干擾調控序列，從而功能性地提升正常基因表達和正常蛋白功能。透過 HDR 修復的編輯，包括目標插入，旨在修正或取代異常的 DNA 序列。疾病的遺傳驅動因素的多樣性需要多樣的解決方案。基因編輯有潛力提供多種類型的基因組修訂，以應對廣泛的疾病。

CRISPR 技術使用由一種酶（稱為 DNA 內切酶）與 RNA 分子（稱為 guide RNA）組成的蛋白-RNA 結合複合物，該 guide RNA 被設計用以識別特定的 DNA 序列。DNA 內切酶是一種會切割 DNA 的酶。此 DNA 內切酶與 guide RNA 的組合僅在兩個條件都滿足時才會結合並切割 DNA：第一，蛋白質會識別一種特定於該酶的短 DNA 序列，稱為 protospacer adjacent motif（"PAM"）；第二，guide RNA 的適當部分會與相鄰的 DNA 序列匹配。被 DNA 內切酶識別的 PAM 序列會在 guide RNA 之外，形成第二層識別。本公司認為 CRISPR 技術在基因編輯方面有三個主要優勢：

• 快速、全面且系統的產品候選人識別。內切酶（無論是 Cas9 或 Cas12a）的主要目標機制是 guide RNA，該 guide RNA 可以迅速替換為不同的 guide RNA 或透過單個核苷酸的變化進行優化。這允許為每個遺傳目標設計、合成並測試數百種 guide RNA/內切酶組合，以找到那些能以最佳效率和特異性切割 DNA 目標的組合。相較之下，其他常用於基因編輯的 DNA 核酸酶在靈活性上本質上受到限制。例如，鋅指核酸酶、工程設計的 meganucleases 及轉錄活化類效應核酸酶使用蛋白質來識別 DNA 序列，以將內切酶帶到基因組中需要切割的位置，這需要為每個目標位點創造全新的蛋白質。

我們是一家先驅基因編輯公司，致力於開發具潛在變革性基因組藥物，以治療廣泛的嚴重疾病。我們已開發出基於CRISPR技術的專有基因編輯平台，並持續擴展其功能。我們的產品開發策略是針對那些基因編輯可用以改善或提升患者治療結果的疾病，同時最大化技術、法規及商業成功的機率。我們專注於開發體內基因編輯藥物，利用功能上調，旨在增加正常基因拷貝及其正常蛋白功能的表達，以治療由遺傳變異所導致、消除或幹擾正常功能的疾病。我們認為，能夠提供體內基因編輯，即藥物經注射或輸注至患者體內，以編輯其體內細胞，並功能上調正常基因表達及正常蛋白功能於目標組織，這項能力有潛力大幅擴展基於CRISPR的基因編輯的治療可能性。為此，我們的預臨牀努力也專注於建立一個 "plug ‘n play" 的脂質奈米粒子 ("LNP") 平台，以實現體內基因編輯藥物針對多種細胞與組織的定向遞送，包括肝臟、造血幹細胞 ("HSCs")，以及其他細胞與組織。

2025年9月，我們宣佈提名我們的體內開發領先候選藥物 EDIT-401，這是一種實驗性、潛在最佳等級、一次療法，用以顯著降低低密度脂蛋白膽固醇 ("LDL-C")，透過上調低密度脂蛋白受體 ("LDLR")。EDIT-401 設計用以治療 LDL-C 水平升高，即高血脂症，透過直接編輯 LDLR 基因的非編碼區域，增加 LDLR 蛋白表達並降低 LDL-C 水準。這種針對性方法在我們的預臨牀研究中已顯示在非人靈長類動物 ("NHPs") 中平均降低 LDL-C 約 90%，且耐受性數據良好，這支持 EDIT-401 有潛力為目前血脂降低療法未充分服務的患者提供

有意義的臨牀結果。我們預計在 2026 年中提交新藥臨牀試驗申請 ("IND") 或其外國對應文件，以進行 EDIT-401 在異質家族性高膽固醇血癥患者的臨牀試驗，並預期在 2026 年底前取得 EDIT-401 的早期人體概念驗證數據。我們計畫在 2027 年完成第一個入體臨牀試驗的劑量尋找部分，並於 2027 年取得初步數據結果。我們預期在 2026 年中展示更多 EDIT-401 的預臨牀數據。

我們的發現與開發努力也包括 HSCs 及其他細胞與組織。基於我們在 renizgamglogene autogedtemcel ("reni-cel") 的臨牀試驗經驗，我們已在 NHPs 中取得體內預臨牀概念驗證數據。此外，我們先前已宣佈在人類化小鼠中透過我們專有的 LNP 定向平台，實現對兩種額外細胞類型的體內遞送，顯示我們專有的非肝臟 LNP 平台具有 "plug ‘n play" 潛力。我們計畫繼續優化 HSC 程式候選藥物，並探討其他細胞與組織的開發，但計畫將資源集中在我們領先的 EDIT-401 程式的人體概念驗證上。

我們透過內部開發及取得補充性技術的授權，追求基因編輯與定向遞送工具的正確組合，以建立預臨牀管道並加速實現為患有先前無法治療疾病的患者提供救命藥物的目標。透過取得補充性技術的授權，我們可以擴展現有的基因編輯平台，並進一步推動體內管道的發展。這在 2024 年我們與某公司簽訂合作與授權協議，以取得針對肝臟的 LNP 技術，包括我們 EDIT-401 程式中使用的 LNP 這一點得到體現。我們也積極尋求機會授權及合作我們強大的智慧財產權組合，以推動 CRISPR 基因編輯藥物在非核心專注領域的發展，並提供非稀釋性資金。例如，我們透過合作進展工程細胞藥物以治療各種癌症，包括與 Bristol Myers Squibb 公司 ("BMS") 透過其全資子公司 Juno Therapeutics, Inc. ("Juno Therapeutics") 的合作。此合作利用我們的 Cas9 和 AsCas12a 平台技術，旨在推動 alpha-beta T 細胞實驗性藥物以治療實體瘤、液體瘤及自身免疫疾病，目前已產生 14 個總計計畫，包括 BMS 的 CD19 HD Allo CAR T 程式，用以治療自身免疫疾病，目前處於第一期臨牀開發階段。

此外，於2023年12月，本公司與Vertex Pharmaceuticals Incorporated（"Vertex"）簽訂授權協議（"Vertex授權協議"），根據該協議，Vertex取得本公司Cas9基因編輯技術的非獨佔授權，用於針對SCD及TDT中BCL11A基因的ex vivo基因編輯藥物，包括Vertex的CASGEVYTM（exagamglogene autotemcel）。本公司於2023年第四季收到224 百萬美元現金預付款，並於2024年第一季收到2024年度授權費10 百萬美元。Vertex授權協議進一步規定Vertex需支付潛在額外50 百萬美元的條件性預付款，以及未來固定及銷售基數年度授權費，範圍每年為5 百萬美元至40 百萬美元，包含某些銷售基數年度授權費的增加，至2034年為止。本公司需支付The Broad Institute, Inc.（"Broad"）及President and Fellows of Harvard College（"Harvard"）中雙位數百分比的金額，該金額為本公司從Vertex取得的授權協議中與Cas9技術相關的付款，該技術由本公司從Broad及Harvard取得授權。於2024年10月，本公司與DRI Healthcare Trust的 wholly owned subsidiary（"DRI"）簽訂協議（"DRI協議"），根據該協議，DRI向本公司支付57 百萬美元現金預付款。根據DRI協議，DRI將購買本公司根據Vertex授權協議有權收取的未來固定及銷售基數年度授權費，該費用每年為5 百萬美元至40 百萬美元，包含基於銷售的增加。此外，DRI將購買本公司可能根據Vertex授權協議收取的50 百萬美元條件性預付款的中雙位數百分比。上述所有金額將調整以排除本公司對Broad及Harvard的付款。本公司保留某些其他銷售基數年度授權費及可能到期的條件性預付款的權利，這些金額與本公司作為授權人的義務相應。

截至目前為止，本公司業務重點為組織及僱用員工、業務規劃、籌集資金、建立智慧財產權組合、組建基因編輯核心能力、尋找潛在產品候選物、並進行臨牀前研究及臨牀試驗。所有持續進行的研究計畫仍處於臨牀前或研究階段，所有研究計畫失敗的風險很高。本公司尚未從產品銷售中產生任何收入。本公司主要透過各種權益融資、與BMS的合作研究付款、前戰略聯盟Allergan Pharmaceuticals International Limited（連同其附屬公司，"Allergan"）的付款（該聯盟於2020年8月終止）、與Vertex授權協議相關的DRI協議付款，以及Vertex授權協議下的付款來資助運作。

自成立以來，本公司已產生顯著的營運虧損。本公司截至2025年12月31日及2024年12月31日的淨虧損分別為160.1 百萬美元及237.1 百萬美元。截至2025年12月31日，本公司累計虧損為1,600 百萬美元。本公司預期將持續產生顯著的費用及營運虧損，至少在可預見的未來。本公司淨虧損可能從季度到季度、從年度到年度大幅波動。本公司預期費用將隨著我們持續支持臨牀前研究及準備EDIT-401的臨牀開發；啟動並進行EDIT-401的臨牀試驗；繼續目前的研究計畫及臨牀前開發活動；尋找其他研究計畫及其他產品候選物；啟動並進行我們識別及開發的其他產品候選物的臨牀前測試；維護、擴展及保護智慧財產權組合，包括償還我們從 licensors 取得的智慧財產權相關費用；進一步發展我們的基因編輯平台；以及聘僱人員而增加。本公司不預期在2026年12月31日結算年度或可預見的未來實現盈利。
截至目前為止，本公司尚未從產品銷售中產生任何收入，且預期在可預見的未來也不會從產品銷售中產生任何收入。

根據與BMS的合作協議，本公司已收到總計159.0 百萬美元的付款，主要為初始預付款及修正付款、開發里程碑付款、研究資金支持及某些選擇權費用。本公司已不再收到研究資金支持。在截至2025年12月31日的會計年度中，本公司確認與BMS合作相關的收入為23.2 百萬美元，其中9.7 百萬美元為先前遞延收入。截至2025年12月31日，本公司與BMS相關的遞延收入為40.5 百萬美元，全部列為長期遞延收入於合併資產負債表中。根據此合作協議，本公司在交付選項包給BMS或收到開發里程碑付款時確認收入。本公司預期收入將因交付選項包或收到里程碑付款的時間而從季度到季度、從年度到年度波動。

根據Vertex授權協議，本公司於2023年第四季簽訂協議時收到50.0 百萬美元現金預付款，並於2024年及2025年第一季分別收到每年10.0 百萬美元的年度授權費。該授權協議進一步規定Vertex需支付潛在額外50.0 百萬美元的條件性預付款，以及未來固定及銷售基數年度授權費，範圍每年為5.0 百萬美元至40.0 百萬美元，包含某些銷售基數年度授權費的增加，至2034年為止。截至2025年12月31日，本公司根據協議記錄的年度授權費收入為10.0 百萬美元。

headings: 與本公司財務狀況相關的風險及對額外資金的需求
自設立以來，本公司已產生重大虧損。本公司預期在可預見的未來將持續產生虧損，並可能永遠無法達成或維持獲利。
本公司將需要大量額外資金。若本公司無法在需要時籌集資金，將被迫延宕、減少或終止本公司研究與產品開發計畫或商業化努力。
籌集額外資金可能導致股東持股稀釋，限制本公司營運或要求本公司放棄對本公司技術或產品候選藥物的權利。
本公司營運歷史可能使股東難以評估本公司業務至今的成功程度，並評估本公司未來的生存能力。
本公司從未自產品銷售中產生收入，並可能永遠無法獲利。
不利的國家或全球經濟情勢或政治發展可能對本公司業務、財務狀況或營運成果產生負面影響。
與發現、開發及商業化相關的風險
管制遺傳藥物的規範，特別是任何我們可能開發的新興遺傳藥物，已頻繁變更，且可能在未來持續變更。
我們可能無法成功進行識別、開發或商業化潛在產品候選藥物的相關努力。
我們尚未在臨牀試驗中測試任何我們提出的遞送方式與產品候選藥物的組合，也尚未在目前的開發計畫中啟動任何臨牀試驗。
我們目前計畫進行並可能在未來於美國境外進行產品候選藥物的臨牀試驗，且美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）及相應的外國監管機關可能不接受來自這些試驗的資料。
經驗到完成開發與商業化這些產品候選藥物的延遲，或最終無法完成開發與商業化這些產品候選藥物。
paragraphs: 本公司業務面臨許多風險。以下重要因素，及其他因素，可能導致本公司實際結果與本年度10-K申報書及其他向美國證券交易委員會（SEC）提交的文件、新聞稿、與投資者溝通內容及口頭陳述中所作的預測有重大差異。實際未來結果可能與預期的預測有重大差異。本公司不負有任何更新預測陳述的義務，無論是因新資訊、未來事件或其他原因。

自設立以來，我們已產生顯著的營運虧損。我們的淨虧損為 160.1 百萬美元、237.1 百萬美元及 153.2 百萬美元，分別為 2025 年 12 月 31 日、2024 年 12 月 31 日及 2023 年 12 月 31 日所終結之會計年度。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們累計虧損為 1.6 十億美元。我們主要透過公開發行本公司普通股、與 Bristol Myers Squibb Company（"BMS"）之研究合作，透過其全資子公司 Juno Therapeutics, Inc.、我們前項戰略聯盟 Allergan Pharmaceuticals International Limited（與其附屬公司合稱 "Allergan"）之付款，該聯盟於 2020 年 8 月終止、我們與 DRI Healthcare Acquisitions LP 之買賣協議所收到之付款，以及我們與 Vertex Pharmaceuticals, Incorporated（"Vertex"）之授權協議所收到之付款，來支應我們之營運。我們已將 substantially all 之努力投入研究與開發。我們預期將持續產生顯著之費用及增加之營運虧損，於可預見之未來。我們所產生之淨虧損可能自季度至季度大幅波動。我們預期，若我們：
• 繼續支持預臨牀研究並為EDIT-401的臨牀開發做準備；
• 開始並執行EDIT-401的臨牀試驗；
• 繼續目前的研究計畫及目前研究計畫中的預臨牀開發產品候選物；
• 嘗試尋找額外的產品候選物及研究計畫；
